claims.text: Anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior in HfNbTaTiZr is caused by an internally generated residual-stress field.
The residual-stress field develops from nanoscale thermal-expansion mismatch between highly distorted or early-stage precipitate regions and a less-distorted matrix.
Internal residual stresses pin dislocations and counteract thermal softening.
HfNbTaTiZr displays elevated-temperature softening resistance and unusually weak temperature dependence of its elastic response.
The initial as-cast HfNbTaTiZr is a single-phase BCC alloy.
The initial alloy contains inherent lattice distortion and nanoscale heterogeneity.
Controlled cold rolling and aging can vary lattice distortion and nanoprecipitation.
A minor alloying addition can reduce differences in thermal-expansion coefficient among local regions.
The relevant strength and modulus plateaus occur between 873 and 1073 K.
Nanoscale distorted regions or nanoprecipitates have a different coefficient of thermal expansion from the surrounding matrix.
Differential expansion during heating and cooling generates internal residual stresses.
Thermally generated residual stresses modify the activation of dislocation glide or climb and reduce the temperature sensitivity of strength and elastic moduli.
Reducing thermal-expansion mismatch will restore more conventional continuous thermomechanical softening.
Samples retaining or enhancing the proposed mismatch will exhibit a high-temperature strength plateau and elevated elastic modulus between 873 and 1073 K.
Samples engineered to reduce the mismatch will soften continuously with increasing temperature.
Dislocation arrangements and local strain fields will correlate with the degree of thermal-expansion or lattice mismatch.
HfNbTaTiZr-derived alloys can exhibit elemental segregation, two BCC phases, and Ta-rich grain-boundary precipitates.
Interstitial oxygen or nitrogen and precipitation are plausible alternative contributors to elevated-temperature mechanical behavior.
Failure of mismatch reduction to change the strength plateau, elastic-modulus behavior, or dislocation structure relative to a control would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as untreated as-cast alloy, whereas the proposed control is described as as-cast followed by cold rolling and aging; these are materially different processing states.
